validation.notes: Repaired three producer/consumer defects in the project-trust path. (1) core/project-trust.ts persisted an extension decision whenever the optional remember field was present; it now persists only when remember === true, so an absent or explicit false remember stays session-only for both approval and denial. (2) core/settings-manager.ts had an inverted guard in setProjectTrusted that returned early exactly when the trust value changed, so granting or revoking trust never reloaded or dropped project settings; the guard now returns only when the value is unchanged. (3) core/resource-loader.ts hard-coded projectTrusted = false after the untrusted bootstrap and never invoked options.resolveProjectTrust, so the resolver never ran and project settings/resources could never become trusted; the resolver now runs exactly once per resolver-carrying reload, receives the bootstrap LoadExtensionsResult, and its boolean is applied via setProjectTrusted before the final settings and extension load. .prale-eval/regression.mjs links the real production modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (project-trust + trust-manager, settings-manager over real files, resource-loader + settings-manager) and fakes only outer boundaries: extension runner aggregation, proper-lockfile, package manager, extension loader/cache, theme/skill/prompt loaders and the event bus. Assertions cover: extension yes/no with absent and remember:false never writing trust.json; remember:true persisting approval and denial and being honoured by later non-interactive sessions; session-only prompt options not persisting while persisted prompt answers do; trustOverride and defaultProjectTrust not persisting; untrusted bootstrap state observed inside the resolver; approval loading project settings and the trust-gated .pi/SYSTEM.md; denial keeping both gated; a later resolver-less reload not re-resolving; and the global agent settings.json bytes staying unchanged. Verified mutation detection: reverting each modified source file alone to its committed baseline fails the script with a distinct assertion (project-trust: 'remember: false must not persist consent'; settings-manager: 'changing trust updates the trust state'; resource-loader: 'the resolver runs exactly once after the untrusted bootstrap'), then the repair is restored and the script passes again. Limitation: the repository's own vitest suite could not be run because no node_modules are installed in this workspace (dependency installation is out of scope); the standalone Node 24 script is the focused validation and executes the real modules. All test inputs are created under .prale-eval/tmp and removed by the script's finally block; no real time, randomness, network or external services are used as evidence (asynchronous ordering is controlled with plain promises).
